$comment: BC Ferries' official GTFS, hosted by Trillium Transit (Mobility Database https://mobilitydatabase.org/feeds/gtfs/mdb-1991, checked 2026-10-28): 23 routes, 96 stops, every major and minor route from Haida Gwaii to the Gulf Islands. No GTFS-realtime: live positions are to come from AIS. The GTFS states no license and BC Ferries publishes no terms for it that we found (DATA-LICENSES.md); used unofficially, without its marks.
name: BC Ferries

static.$comment: Export of 2026-10-09 ('UTC: 09-Oct-2026 16:33'), valid 2026-10-09 to 2027-03-31; calendar.txt with exception-only services, shape_dist_traveled in metres, no block_id on trips (runcut.txt has blocks, but nothing says which vessel runs a sailing).
static.$statedTimezone: agency.txt says America/Los_Angeles, but 51 of its stops say America/Vancouver and its times are BC's (sailings at the published local times, e.g. Tsawwassen 07:00). The two agreed until BC moved to permanent UTC-7 in November 2026 (tzdata 2026b), so read in America/Vancouver.

display.$tripId: Trillium's trip ids are "t_<trip>_b_<calendar>_tn_<n>" (e.g. t_6182680_b_87164_tn_0): the trip number alone.
display.$feedVersion: Versions are Trillium's export time, "UTC: 09-Oct-2026 16:33": the date is enough.

ais.$comment: Live vessel positions from aisstream.io (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#seabus-ais, as for SeaBus): the server's leader keeps one WebSocket open for these vessels, records them to var/ais-history/bc-ferries/, and the browser matches each fix to the sailing on any route it fits best (packages/transit-core/src/ais/match.ts), anchoring the timetable. BC Ferries doesn't own its ships' AIS broadcasts; no BC Ferries data or marks are used for this (DATA-LICENSES.md).
ais.$routes: Every route in the feed: vessels move between routes, so a fix may match any of them.
ais.$vessels: MMSIs and names as heard on aisstream.io over the BC coast for 30 minutes on 2026-10-28 from 17:10 (pipelines/discover-ais.ts --match on BC Ferries' vessel names; workboats with similar names left out). Vessels not heard then (Bowen Queen, Mayne Queen, Quadra Queen II, Powell River Queen, Malaspina Sky, Baynes Sound Connector, Kahloke, Kwuna, Nimpkish, Tachek, Northern Sea Wolf, Island Aurora, Island Discovery, Queen of Chilliwack, Salish Orca, Quinsam) aren't listed yet; their sailings stay timetable estimates. Northern Expedition and Queen of Surrey sent only static data, no positions (config/regions/vancouver-island/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #7).
ais.$boundingBox: The BC coast from the Gulf Islands to Prince Rupert and Haida Gwaii, [[lat, lon], [lat, lon]] (aisstream order).
ais.$coverageGapS: AIS recorder coverage breaks when consecutive batches are further apart than this; batches are sent every batchS while connected, empty or not (as for SeaBus).
ais.$liveWindowS: As for SeaBus (config/feeds/translink/feed.json): longer than the day file's edge-cache time plus the browser's longest poll interval.
ais.$match: Matching fixes to sailings. In the 2026-10-28 probe, vessels reported every 100-500 s (much sparser than SeaBus's ~60 s), and sailings run on GTFS shapes that are only roughly the vessels' tracks. Guesses (config/regions/vancouver-island/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #8).

match.$maxOffsetM: Vessels cross open water, often a kilometre or more off the GTFS shape (guess).
match.$maxShiftS: Major-route sailings run an hour late or more on busy days (guess).
match.$dockRadiusM: A terminal's berths are a few hundred metres apart, and the GTFS stop is one point among them (guess).
match.$minTurnaroundS: Loading and unloading a large ferry takes 20 minutes or more (guess).

ais.$glide: Smoothing when new fixes move a vessel: larger distances than SeaBus's, since fixes are minutes apart (guesses).
